subject.title: fix: workspace divergence no longer wedges cloud-worker sessions

question: Should cloud-worker reconciliation retain a worker after a keep-local conflict only when the accepted base is guaranteed to exist remotely, or should it reclaim/resynchronize that worker before accepting the local manifest?
rationale: The fixed keep-local policy is a durable operator-facing recovery contract, and the safe ownership of a recomputed local manifest versus a retained remote worker cannot be selected mechanically.

options.title: Resynchronize before retaining
options.body: Publish or synchronize the accepted canonical manifest and tree to the worker before committing it as the next base, then prove a subsequent turn succeeds.

options.title: Reclaim after conflict
options.body: Accept the keep-local result but reclaim the divergent worker so the next turn provisions from the canonical local workspace.

options.title: Pause for contract design
options.body: Keep the phase-two PR open while the cloud-worker owner decides the permanent post-conflict worker lifecycle.

recommendation.title: Resynchronize before retaining
recommendation.body: Publish or synchronize the accepted canonical manifest and tree to the worker before committing it as the next base, then prove a subsequent turn succeeds.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged and proposed cloud-worker recovery work connects this person directly to the staged-result and reconciliation lifecycle.
